turns.text: Right — so the migration lock timeout is a safeguard that stops a migration if it can’t get exclusive access to the database within a set period. When a migration starts, it creates a lock entry so no other process runs migrations at the same time. If that lock isn’t released—because the previous run hung, crashed, or is still processing—the next attempt will wait until the timeout expires and then fail. It’s meant to avoid deadlocks and conflicting schema changes. Do you see any long‑running steps or crashes right before the timeout?
